prompt:
Summarize the merged change below in at most two sentences for a changelog: what changed, then why. Name the pull request number exactly as written (#NNNN). Use only facts stated in the change text. Also name the ticket OMN-19980.

--- change 1 (repo omnimarket, pull request #3373) ---
test(OMN-19980): a CI guard holds savings to one definition in SQL (#3373)
* test(OMN-19980): a CI guard holds savings to one definition in SQL

Savings is defined once, in node_metering_summary_compute. Nothing stopped a
second definition from coming back: five applied migrations still spell
'claude-opus-4.1' AS baseline_model, and a later migration could reintroduce a
hard-coded baseline or multiply tokens by a price in SQL without any check
noticing. The live views are already clean (090, 089 and 093 replaced them), so
the guard has to prove that, not assume it.

tests/test_single_savings_definition.py fails on: a string literal feeding a
baseline_model column; the last migration defining any of the three savings
views carrying one; claude-opus-4.1 anywhere under src/ outside the five frozen
history migrations (and a frozen entry that no longer holds it, so the list can
only shrink); SQL, in .sql, Python strings and YAML, that multiplies a token
column by a price outside node_metering_summary_compute; and ci.yml not running
the guard as a named blocking step. That last assertion is what makes the bound
evidence check fail at the merge base for a real reason.

Python price arithmetic is outside the ticket's SQL scope and is asserted as a
known gap, not scanned. 077 holds a placeholder baseline ('cloud-baseline')
that the guard found on the real tree; it is frozen as history, superseded by
089.

contracts/OMN-19980.yaml binds AC1 to the guard.

Onex-
